units.title_th: ทักทายและคำสุภาพ
units.goal_th: ทักทาย ขอบคุณ ขอโทษ และบอกลาเป็นภาษาเกาหลีได้
units.scenario: B is Minjun, Nam's Korean friend, met on campus and again after teacher Lee's class. Nam greets him casually and politely, asks how he is, thanks him, asks how to say a Thai word in Korean, and says goodbye and good night the right way.

lessons.topic: Greeting friends; a lighter thank-you; good night; what to say when leaving a shop or an office
lessons.grammar: Casual vs polite: 안녕 (friends, younger people) vs 안녕하세요; -요 keeps a phrase polite (고마워요 is softer than 감사합니다); 잘 지내요? as a question (rising) and 잘 지내요 as the answer (falling); 수고하세요 to people at work. Stage A dialogues use stage A words only (있어요, 어디, 가요, 좋아해요 come in stage B)

lessons.topic: Classroom phrases: saying you have a question, asking how to say something in Korean, the teacher's "repeat after me", confirming that you know or that something is right
lessons.grammar: N + (으)로 "in (a language)": 한국어로 뭐예요?; 질문 있어요 as a fixed phrase; 알아요 vs 몰라요 (review); 맞아요 to confirm

units.title_th: อักษรฮันกึล 1
units.goal_th: อ่านสระพื้นฐานและพยัญชนะ ㄱ ㄴ ㄷ ㄹ ㅁ ได้
units.scenario: B is a Korean tutor with hangul flashcards. Nam reads aloud syllables and short words made only of the basic vowels and ㄱ ㄴ ㄷ ㄹ ㅁ (나무, 누구, 오리, 고구마) and asks what they mean.

lessons.topic: Reading practice: ㄱ ㄴ ㄷ ㄹ ㅁ with ㅡ and ㅣ, then whole words built only from the letters learned so far
lessons.grammar: Syllable blocks: consonant + vertical vowel side by side (기, 니), + horizontal vowel stacked (그); read words block by block (나-무, 오-리); ㄱ between vowels sounds voiced (누구 = นู-กู)

lessons.topic: Reading practice: the y-vowels ㅑ ㅕ ㅛ ㅠ after consonants, and everyday words that use only the letters learned so far
lessons.grammar: y-vowels after a consonant (교 as in 학교, 뉴 as in 메뉴); three-syllable words (고구마); 이모 is also how people call a restaurant auntie

units.title_th: แนะนำตัว
units.goal_th: บอกชื่อ สัญชาติ และอาชีพของตัวเอง และถามคนอื่นได้
units.scenario: B is Minjun at a language-exchange party with international students. Nam introduces themself (name, nationality, student), asks where the others are from and which languages they speak, and answers modestly when praised for their Korean.

lessons.topic: Classmates from other countries: China, the USA, Vietnam, the UK; the word for foreigner
lessons.grammar: Country + 사람 (review: 중국 사람이에요); 어느 나라 사람이에요? (review); many country names end in 국 "country" (한국, 중국, 미국, 영국)

lessons.topic: Languages: which languages you speak, a little or well; answering a compliment on your Korean politely
lessons.grammar: Language = country + 어 (태국어, 중국어; but 영어); N + 말해요; 조금 / 잘 before the verb; reply to praise with 아니에요 (Korean modesty, like Thai ไม่หรอก)

units.title_th: อักษรฮันกึล 2
units.goal_th: อ่านพยัญชนะครบทุกตัวและสระผสมได้ ฟังแยกเสียงธรรมดา เสียงพ่นลม และเสียงเกร็งออก
units.scenario: B is a Korean tutor reading words aloud. Nam says which sound was heard (plain, aspirated or tense: 가/카/까) and reads short words that use every consonant and the compound vowels (포도, 토끼, 아저씨, 시계, 회사).

lessons.topic: Reading words with plain, aspirated and tense consonants (no final consonants yet)
lessons.grammar: Plain / aspirated / tense inside real words: 포도 (ㅍ), 토끼 (ㅌ + ㄲ), 아저씨 (ㅆ), 바빠요 (ㅂ + ㅃ), 피자 (ㅍ + ㅈ), 따로 (ㄸ); ㅈ ㅂ become voiced between vowels

lessons.topic: Reading words with compound vowels and ㅖ
lessons.grammar: ㅖ after a consonant sounds like ㅔ (시계); ㅐ and ㅔ sound alike (가게, 노래); ㅙ ㅟ ㅚ in short words (왜, 위, 회사)

units.title_th: ตัวเลขและอายุ
units.goal_th: นับเลขได้ทั้งสองชุด บอกเบอร์โทรและอายุได้
units.scenario: B is a staff member at a Korean language school in Bangkok, signing Nam up for a class. He asks Nam's age and phone number (a Thai number) and tells Nam the classroom number and the floor; Nam asks his age politely and uses the right number system each time.

lessons.topic: Ages over 20: native Korean tens (30, 40, 50, 60) and the polite way to ask an older person's age
lessons.grammar: Native tens + 살 (서른 살, 마흔다섯 살); 스물/서른 + 하나… for 21, 31 (스물한 살); 나이가 어떻게 되세요? (honorific) vs 몇 살이에요?

lessons.topic: Numbers on things: floors, room numbers, numbered items; asking "what number?" and "which floor?"
lessons.grammar: Sino-Korean number + 층 / 호 / 번 (삼 층, 칠 호, 이 번); 몇 + counter to ask (몇 층이에요?); 지하 일 층 = B1

units.title_th: กินและดื่ม
units.goal_th: สั่งอาหารและเครื่องดื่ม และบอกได้ว่าอร่อยหรือเผ็ด
units.scenario: B is a waiter at a Korean snack restaurant (분식집) in Bangkok. Nam calls him over, orders popular dishes and drinks, asks for more, says whether the food is spicy, sweet or nutty, and says they are full.

lessons.topic: Popular Korean dishes Thai visitors love: gimbap, tteokbokki, samgyeopsal, fried chicken, cold noodles
lessons.grammar: N + 먹어요 / 주세요 (review); 음식 "food": 한국 음식, 태국 음식; ordering portions with native numbers (김밥 하나 주세요)

lessons.topic: Tastes (sweet, nutty) and saying you are full; what the staff say when they serve food
lessons.grammar: Descriptive verbs at the end of the sentence (떡볶이가 달아요); 배고파요 ↔ 배불러요; 맛있게 드세요 (staff) ↔ 잘 먹겠습니다 (customer)

units.title_th: สีและรูปทรง
units.goal_th: บอกสีและรูปทรงของสิ่งต่าง ๆ ถามว่าสีอะไร และบอกว่ายาว สั้น หนัก เบา เหมือนหรือต่างกันได้
units.scenario: B is a shop assistant in a small Korean stationery and gift shop in Bangkok. Nam asks what colour things are, says which colour and shape they want (a red heart, a yellow star), and compares items: long or short, heavy or light, the same or different, bright or dark.

lessons.topic: Basic colours: red, blue, yellow; asking what colour something is
lessons.grammar: 무슨 색이에요? → 빨간색이에요 (N이에요 review); colour words = colour + 색. Stage A dialogues use stage A words only (있어요, 어디, 가요, 좋아해요, 커요 come in stage B)

lessons.topic: White, black, green, purple, pink
lessons.grammar: N은/는 N색이에요 (바지는 까만색이에요); colour words end in a consonant, so they take 이에요; 핑크색 is an English loanword

lessons.topic: More colours: brown, orange, sky blue, navy
lessons.grammar: N도 + colour (바지도 남색이에요); 하늘색 = 하늘 "sky" + 색, like Thai สีฟ้า

lessons.topic: Describing things: long or short, heavy or light
lessons.grammar: N이/가 + descriptive verb with no word for "is" (바지가 길어요, 의자가 무거워요); 무거워요/가벼워요 learned as whole words

lessons.topic: The same or different; bright or dark colours
lessons.grammar: N하고 N이/가 같아요 / 달라요 (하고 = and); 밝아요 / 어두워요 for colours and rooms

lessons.topic: Shapes: circle, square, triangle, heart, star
lessons.grammar: N이에요 with colour + shape (빨간색 하트예요); 동그라미 also means the O mark for a correct answer, like Thai ถูก ✓

units.title_th: ของใช้รอบตัว
units.goal_th: ถามว่านี่คืออะไร เป็นของใคร อยู่ตรงไหน และบอกชื่อของใช้ประจำวันได้
units.scenario: B is Minjun at a café table covered with both their things. They point at objects (이게 뭐예요?), ask whose they are, say where they are (on, under, inside, between), and Nam asks to borrow something.

lessons.topic: What is this / that? Naming everyday objects
lessons.grammar: 이게 뭐예요? (이게 = this + subject 이); 그거 (near you) / 저거 (over there) like Thai นั่น / โน่น; 뭐 = what. Stage A dialogues use stage A words only

lessons.topic: Whose is it? Mine! Phones and wallets
lessons.grammar: 누구 거예요? → 제 거예요 / 민준 씨 거예요 (N + 거 = N's one); 제 = my (polite form of 저)

lessons.topic: Things you carry every day: umbrella, glasses, tissues, water bottle, keys
lessons.grammar: N이에요? 네/아니요 (review); N도 (우산도 제 거예요)

lessons.topic: Things on the table; asking to borrow something
lessons.grammar: N 빌려주세요 (please lend me N) vs N 주세요 (please give me N)

lessons.topic: Where is it? On, under, inside, between; looking for something
lessons.grammar: N 위/아래/안이에요 (지갑은 테이블 위예요, 핸드폰은 의자 아래예요); 위 from ko-A4-06; N 찾아요

lessons.topic: Toiletries for the dorm or a trip: soap, toothbrush, toothpaste, shampoo, razor
lessons.grammar: N 주세요 / N이에요? (review) at a shop or with a roommate; 칫솔 + 치약 share 치 "tooth"

units.title_th: ในห้องเรียน
units.goal_th: บอกชื่ออุปกรณ์การเรียนและของในห้องเรียน และพูดเรื่องการเรียนภาษาเกาหลีง่าย ๆ ได้
units.scenario: B is a Korean classmate on Nam's first day at a Korean language school. He asks to borrow a pencil or an eraser, asks about the textbook and the homework, they talk about whether Korean is easy, difficult or fun, and they make a card together in class.

lessons.topic: Stationery: pencil, ballpoint pen, notebook, eraser, pencil case
lessons.grammar: N 빌려주세요 / N 주세요 (review); 이게 뭐예요? (review). Stage A dialogues use stage A words only

lessons.topic: In the classroom: classroom, desk, whiteboard, textbook, dictionary
lessons.grammar: N이에요 / N이/가 아니에요 (review); 책상 위, 의자 아래 (review of ko-A8-05)

lessons.topic: Is Korean difficult? Easy, difficult, fun, boring
lessons.grammar: N이/가 + descriptive verb (한글이 쉬워요, 한국어가 재미있어요); 재미있어요 ↔ 재미없어요 work like 맛있어요 ↔ 맛없어요

lessons.topic: Study verbs: write, learn, teach, practise, ask
lessons.grammar: N + verb (한글 써요, 한국어 배워요; the object marker can be dropped in speech); 써요 also means "use" and "wear (a hat)"

lessons.topic: Homework and tests; when things start and finish
lessons.grammar: N이/가 시작해요 / 끝나요 (시험이 시작해요, 숙제가 끝나요?); 문제가 어려워요 (review)

lessons.topic: Making a card in class: scissors, glue, ruler, coloured pencils, paper
lessons.grammar: N 주세요 / N 빌려주세요 (review); 색연필 = 색 + 연필, read [생년필]

units.title_th: บ้านและห้อง
units.goal_th: บอกชื่อห้องและของใช้ในบ้าน และบรรยายห้องของตัวเองง่าย ๆ ได้
units.scenario: B is Minjun on a video call. He asks to see Nam's flat; Nam names the rooms and furniture, says where things are, describes the room (small but clean, quiet) and shows the shoe cabinet and mailbox at the entrance.

lessons.topic: Rooms of a home: room, living room, bedroom, bathroom
lessons.grammar: N이에요 (point and name: 거실이에요); Korean homes: shoes come off at the door. Stage A dialogues use stage A words only

lessons.topic: Furniture: bed, sofa, drawers, dressing table
lessons.grammar: N 위 / 아래 / 안 / 사이 (침대 위, 서랍 안) (review of ko-A8-05)

lessons.topic: In the bedroom: blanket, pillow, curtains, TV, electric fan
lessons.grammar: N이에요 / N이/가 아니에요 (review); loanwords (텔레비전, 커튼) vs native words (이불, 베개); 선풍기 = electric fan

lessons.topic: Door, window, wall, floor, light
lessons.grammar: N이/가 밝아요 / 어두워요 (방이 밝아요, from ko-A7-05); 불 = light (and fire); Korean homes heat the floor (바닥, ondol)

lessons.topic: Describing a room: spacious or small, clean or dirty, quiet
lessons.grammar: N이/가 + descriptive verb (방이 좁아요); 은/는 to contrast two things (방은 좁아요. 거실은 넓어요.)

lessons.topic: Where do you live? Apartments, the shoe cabinet, mailboxes, the management office
lessons.grammar: N에 살아요 (아파트에 살아요; 에 = in/at); N 몇 층이에요? (review of ko-A5-06)

units.title_th: คนรอบตัว
units.goal_th: เรียกและพูดถึงคนรอบตัวอย่างสุภาพ เช่น ผู้ชาย ผู้หญิง เด็ก คนนี้ คนนั้น เพื่อน และคนทำงานต่าง ๆ ได้
units.scenario: B is a Korean friend looking at photos on Nam's phone from a campus festival. He asks who the people are (이분은 누구예요?); Nam says whether they are men, women or children, friends or classmates, what they look like (long or short hair, glasses) and what they do (a cook, a delivery rider, a soldier).

lessons.topic: Men, women, children, people
lessons.grammar: N이에요 / N이/가 아니에요 (review); 들 makes a plural when needed (사람들), often left out in Korean, as in Thai. Stage A dialogues use stage A words only

lessons.topic: This person, that person: polite words for people
lessons.grammar: 이분/그분/저분 = this/that person (polite, for adults), 그 사람 (neutral); 이분은 누구예요? (누구 from ko-A2-05)

lessons.topic: Addressing people: everyone, ma'am, miss, customers
lessons.grammar: 여러분 to a group (like ทุกคน); 아주머니 (polite) for a middle-aged woman, 아저씨 (from ko-A4-05) for a man; 아가씨 = young lady (calling a waitress 아가씨 can sound rude today: use 저기요); 손님 = customer, guest

lessons.topic: Friends: boyfriend, girlfriend, classmates, being close
lessons.grammar: N이에요 (제 반 친구예요); 친해요 = we are close; 남자 친구 / 여자 친구 are written with a space

lessons.topic: What people look like: long hair, short hair, wearing glasses, smiling
lessons.grammar: Modifier chunks 긴 머리 / 짧은 머리 + 이에요; 안경을 써요 (써요 from ko-A9-04); 웃어요

lessons.topic: People at work: shop assistant, security guard, delivery rider, cook, soldier
lessons.grammar: Job + 이에요 (review of ko-A3-04: 회사원이에요); 원 / 사 in job words (경비원, 배달원, 요리사)

units.title_th: คำยืมจากภาษาอังกฤษ
units.goal_th: อ่านและพูดคำยืมจากภาษาอังกฤษที่คนเกาหลีใช้ทุกวัน และเข้าใจว่าเสียงเปลี่ยนไปอย่างไร
units.scenario: B is a Korean student playing a guessing game with Nam: he says English loanwords the Korean way (컴퓨터, 햄버거, 오렌지, 셀카) and Nam guesses the English word and uses it in a short sentence (N이에요, N 주세요); then they swap roles.

lessons.topic: Computer words: computer, laptop, mouse, earphones
lessons.grammar: How English sounds become hangul: f/p → ㅍ (컴퓨터), final consonants get 으 (마우스), "laptop" is 노트북 in Korean. Stage A dialogues use stage A words only

lessons.topic: Fast food: hamburger, sandwich, salad, spaghetti
lessons.grammar: N 주세요 / N 먹어요 (review); stress-free Korean rhythm: every syllable gets the same length (햄-버-거)

lessons.topic: Sweets and cheese: chocolate, cookies, jelly, cheese
lessons.grammar: z/j → ㅈ (치즈, 젤리); N이/가 달아요 (review of ko-A6-06)

lessons.topic: Fruit with English names: orange, lemon, kiwi, tomato
lessons.grammar: N이에요 / N 주세요; l → ㄹㄹ in the middle of a word (젤리, 샐러드); the colour of fruit (오렌지는 주황색이에요, from ko-A7-03)

lessons.topic: Made-in-Korea English and media words: selfie, power socket, news, sports
lessons.grammar: Konglish: 셀카 (self + camera = selfie), 콘센트 (= power socket, not "consent"); 뉴스, 스포츠 as everyday words

lessons.topic: Stationery with English names: notebook, pen, tape, stickers
lessons.grammar: 노트 = notebook (also 공책 from ko-A9-01); N 주세요 / N 빌려주세요 (review)

units.title_th: ผักและผลไม้
units.goal_th: บอกชื่อผักและผลไม้ที่เห็นบ่อยในเกาหลีและไทย และซื้อผักผลไม้ง่าย ๆ ได้
units.scenario: B is the owner of a Korean grocery shop in Bangkok that sells fruit and vegetables. Nam names fruits and vegetables, asks what something is (이게 뭐예요?), says which fruit is the most delicious, and buys a few things (N 주세요).

lessons.topic: Korean fruits: strawberry, watermelon, tangerine, peach, Korean melon
lessons.grammar: N 주세요 / N이에요 (review); 참외 is a yellow Korean melon eaten in summer. Stage A dialogues use stage A words only

lessons.topic: Tropical fruits and fresh juice: dragon fruit, pineapple, pear, fresh fruit juice
lessons.grammar: N이/가 달아요 / 맛있어요 (review); 배 = pear (also stomach: same sound, different meaning); 생과일 주스 = 생 "fresh" + 과일 + 주스

lessons.topic: Vegetables 1: carrot, potato, onion, ginger
lessons.grammar: N하고 N 주세요 (당근하고 감자 주세요); 오이 from ko-A2-01 and 고구마 from ko-A2-06 (review)

lessons.topic: Vegetables 2: chili pepper, mushroom, napa cabbage, corn
lessons.grammar: N이/가 매워요 (고추가 매워요, review); 배추 is the cabbage used for kimchi

lessons.topic: Spring onion, pumpkin, beans; fresh; the most delicious
lessons.grammar: 제일 + descriptive verb (수박이 제일 맛있어요); 싱싱해요 = fresh (fruit, vegetables, fish)

lessons.topic: Greens for Korean barbecue: lettuce, perilla leaves, bean sprouts, spinach
lessons.grammar: N하고 N (상추하고 깻잎, review); Koreans wrap grilled meat in 상추 and 깻잎 (깻잎 is read [깬닙])

units.title_th: ร้านค้าในเมือง
units.goal_th: บอกชื่อร้านค้าแบบต่าง ๆ และรู้ว่าจะซื้ออะไรที่ร้านไหน
units.scenario: B is Minjun showing Nam the shops in the Korean Town area of Bangkok. They point at shops (빵집, 서점, 분식집…), say what each shop is and what it sells, and Nam says what they need there (N 주세요 / N이에요?).

lessons.topic: Shops 1: bakery, flower shop, bookshop, stationery shop
lessons.grammar: Shop words end in 집 / 점 (빵집, 꽃집, 서점, 문구점); 저거 빵집이에요? (review of ko-A8-01). Stage A dialogues use stage A words only

lessons.topic: Shops 2: supermarket, butcher's, optician's, clothes shop
lessons.grammar: N이에요? 네/아니요 (review); 가게 = shop (from ko-A4-06): 옷 가게

lessons.topic: Places to eat: snack bar, barbecue restaurant, fried-chicken place, street stall
lessons.grammar: N이에요 + food (분식집이에요. 떡볶이 맛있어요.); 포장마차 = covered street stall; 고깃집 = 고기 + 집

lessons.topic: Shops for daily needs: phone shop, photo studio, PC room, fruit shop
lessons.grammar: 사진관 for ID photos; 피시방 = PC room (Korean gaming café); N이에요 (review)

lessons.topic: More shops: shoe shop, cosmetics shop, furniture shop, hardware store
lessons.grammar: Compound shop names (신발 가게, 화장품 가게, 가구점, 철물점); N 주세요 (review)

lessons.topic: Big stores and small shops: open 24 hours, department store, part-timer, owner
lessons.grammar: Number + 시간 (이십사 시간); 주인 = owner, 아르바이트생 = part-time worker (Korean 아르바이트 comes from German "Arbeit")

units.title_th: ป้ายที่เห็นบ่อย
units.goal_th: อ่านและเข้าใจป้ายสำคัญในสถานี ร้านค้า และอาคารได้
units.scenario: B is a Korean tourist in Bangkok who asks Nam about the signs in a Korean restaurant and a department store with Korean signs. Nam reads signs aloud (나가는 곳, 타는 곳, 공사 중, 휴무…) and checks what they mean or whether it is the right place (나가는 곳이에요?).

lessons.topic: Subway signs: way out, platform, transfer, emergency exit
lessons.grammar: Sign phrases with -는 곳 "place where you …" (나가는 곳, 타는 곳, 갈아타는 곳) learned as chunks; N이에요? 네/아니요. Stage A dialogues use stage A words only

lessons.topic: In buildings: lift, escalator, smoking room, toilet paper
lessons.grammar: Formal sign words (승강기 = lift) vs everyday loanwords (에스컬레이터); 지하 일 층 (review of ko-A5-06)

lessons.topic: Doors and shops: push, pull, open, close, open for business
lessons.grammar: Sign commands with -(으)세요 (미세요, 당기세요); 열어요 / 닫아요 as verbs; 영업 중 = open now

lessons.topic: Not available: closed day, under construction, out of order, occupied
lessons.grammar: N 중 = "in the middle of N" (공사 중, 사용 중); 고장 = broken, out of order

lessons.topic: Information and tickets: ticket, information desk, stop, caution
lessons.grammar: Sign nouns without endings (정지, 주의); 표 주세요 (review of 주세요)

lessons.topic: Warning signs: danger, no entry, be quiet, do not touch
lessons.grammar: Fixed sign phrases: -지 마세요 "don't" (만지지 마세요) and -(으)세요 "please" (조용히 하세요); 출입 금지 = no entry

units.title_th: คำอุทานและคำพูดติดปาก
units.goal_th: ตอบสนองด้วยคำอุทาน คำชม และคำให้กำลังใจที่คนเกาหลีพูดบ่อยได้
units.scenario: B is a Korean friend telling Nam surprising news (he passed a test, met a famous singer, lost his phone). Nam reacts with typical exclamations (진짜? 대박! 어떡해!), praises him and encourages him, as in Korean dramas.

lessons.topic: Surprise: really?, awesome!, wow, oh my goodness
lessons.grammar: Intonation: 진짜? (rising) vs 진짜! (falling); 대박 = awesome / huge. Stage A dialogues use stage A words only

lessons.topic: Drama exclamations: oh dear, oh my, no way, you scared me
lessons.grammar: 아이고 (older people, like Thai โอ๊ย), 어머 (mostly women), 헐 (young people, casual), 깜짝이야 (startled)

lessons.topic: Reacting in a conversation: is that so?, really?, of course
lessons.grammar: 그래요? / 정말이에요? to show interest (-요 makes them polite); 물론이죠 / 당연하죠 = of course

lessons.topic: Encouraging and praising: cheer up, well done, good job, the best
lessons.grammar: Set phrases with -세요 / -었어요 learned as chunks (힘내세요, 잘했어요, 수고했어요); N이/가 최고예요!

lessons.topic: When something goes wrong (or right): what do I do?, big trouble, oh right!, what a relief
lessons.grammar: 어떡해 (casual, often in dramas), 큰일 났어요 (fixed past form), 아참 when you remember something, 다행이에요 = what a relief

lessons.topic: Compliments: cool, amazing, I'm jealous, the best (slang)
lessons.grammar: N이/가 멋있어요 / 대단해요; 부러워요 = I envy you (friendly); 짱 is casual slang for "the best"

units.title_th: ตัวสะกดและการเชื่อมเสียง
units.goal_th: อ่านตัวสะกด (받침) ทั้ง 7 เสียงและอ่านเชื่อมเสียงได้ถูกต้อง
units.scenario: B is a Korean tutor. Nam reads aloud words and short sentences full of final consonants and sound changes (한국말, 박물관, 많아요, 못해요), then describes their room with 있어요 / 없어요 and 많아요.

lessons.topic: Nasal assimilation: ㄱ ㄷ ㅂ before ㄴ or ㅁ sound like ㅇ ㄴ ㅁ
lessons.grammar: 비음화: 입니다 → [임니다], 한국말 → [한궁말], 박물관 → [방물관], 막내 → [망내], 콧물 → [콘물]; the formal 입니다 = 이에요

lessons.topic: ㅎ that disappears or makes the next sound aspirated; ㄴ next to ㄹ becomes ㄹ
lessons.grammar: ㅎ is silent before a vowel: 많아요 → [마나요], 싫어요 → [시러요], 놓아요 → [노아요]; ㅎ + ㄷ/ㄱ/ㅂ/ㅈ → aspirated: 못해요 → [모태요]; ㄹ + ㄴ → [ㄹㄹ]: 실내 → [실래]

lessons.topic: Nam describes their dormitory room: the room is small (좁아요) but clean and cosy; there is a bed, a desk and a window with a flowerpot; there are many Korean books but no TV; so for Nam this room is the best (최고예요)
lessons.grammar: Review of 있어요 / 없어요, 많아요, 은/는 for contrast, linking across particles (방이 [방이], 책이 [채기])

units.title_th: วัน เวลา และวันที่
units.goal_th: ถามและบอกวัน วันที่ วันเกิด และเวลาได้
units.scenario: B is Minjun planning a study session with Nam. They ask each other the day and the date, talk about this week, next week and next month, what time classes start and end (from … to …), and agree on a time.

lessons.topic: This week, next week, this month, next month, weekdays, the day after tomorrow
lessons.grammar: 이번 / 다음 + 주 / 달 (이번 주 금요일, 다음 달 오일); 평일 ↔ 주말; 모레 = the day after tomorrow

lessons.topic: From … to …; about (a time); night; being late
lessons.grammar: N부터 N까지 (아홉 시부터 열두 시까지, 월요일부터 금요일까지); time + 쯤 (세 시쯤); 늦어요 = I'm late / it's late

lessons.topic: A notice from Nam's Korean language school: classes run Monday to Friday from 9 to 12; next Wednesday there is no class; a Korean culture day (cooking, hanbok photos) is on Friday afternoon and all students can take part
lessons.grammar: 부터 / 까지, 에 with days and times, N이/가 없어요

units.title_th: ซื้อของและราคา
units.goal_th: ถามราคา นับเงินวอน ต่อราคา และซื้อของได้
units.scenario: B is a shopkeeper at a traditional market and then a cashier at a mart. Nam asks prices, buys things using counters, bargains, gets a free extra (서비스), and pays at the checkout with a trolley and a points card.

lessons.topic: At the traditional market: buying and selling vegetables; getting a free extra
lessons.grammar: N을/를 사요 / 팔아요 (buy / sell); N도 팔아요? (Do you also sell N?); 서비스 = something extra for free, not "service"

lessons.topic: At the checkout of a mart: paying, trolley, points, payment
lessons.grammar: 계산해 주세요 (-아/어 주세요 review); N 있어요? (포인트 카드 있어요?); 결제 = payment (카드 결제, 현금 결제)

lessons.topic: Nam texts Minjun from Dongdaemun market: there are so many shops and the prices are good; T-shirts are only 5,000 won; Nam buys two cheaply (present tense: 싸게 사요); Nam asks which colour Minjun wants and offers to choose one for him
lessons.grammar: Prices with Sino-Korean numbers + 원, the counter 개, -요 questions in a chat message

units.title_th: สถานที่และการเดินทาง
units.goal_th: ถามว่าอยู่ที่ไหน บอกว่าจะไปไหนและไปอย่างไรได้
units.scenario: B is a passer-by near a subway exit in Seoul. Nam asks the way to a place; he gives directions (go straight, cross at the crossroads, turn left) and says which bus or line to take and where to transfer and get off.

lessons.topic: Asking the way: road, straight ahead, crossing, crossroads, corner
lessons.grammar: Direction with (으)로: 왼쪽으로 가세요, 오른쪽으로 가세요; 쭉 가세요; -(으)세요 heard as a polite instruction

lessons.topic: Taking the subway and the bus: getting off, transferring, bus stop, line number, transport card
lessons.grammar: N에서 내려요 / 갈아타요 (place + 에서); 이 호선 = Line 2; 교통 카드 (T-money) works on buses, subways and taxis

lessons.topic: Nam visits Minjun's new home for the first time: takes Line 2, comes out of the wrong exit, a kind man says to go straight, cross at the crossroads and turn at the corner, the building is next to a bank, and after 20 minutes Nam finally arrives
lessons.grammar: A sequence of short 해요체 sentences; 에 / 에서 with places; directions (review)

units.title_th: กิจวัตรประจำวัน
units.goal_th: เล่าว่าทำอะไรบ้างในแต่ละวันและบ่อยแค่ไหน
units.scenario: B is a Korean classmate interviewing Nam for a class project about daily life. He asks what time Nam gets up, what Nam does before leaving home and in the evening, and how often.

lessons.topic: Getting ready in the morning: washing, showering, brushing teeth, putting on make-up, going out
lessons.grammar: N을/를 + verb (이를 닦아요; 이 "teeth" is the same word as the number 이); time + 에 (review); one action per sentence

lessons.topic: Evening at home: coming home, cleaning, homework; early and late
lessons.grammar: Noun + 해요 verbs (청소해요, 숙제해요); 들어와요 = come (back) home; 일찍 ↔ 늦게 before the verb

lessons.topic: Nam's diary for a busy Monday: gets up at 6:30, showers, eats breakfast, studies at school in the morning, works at a café in the afternoon, cleans in the evening, rests a little and goes to bed late; a very long day
lessons.grammar: Time + 에, place + 에서, frequency words in a diary

units.title_th: ครอบครัวและความรู้สึก
units.goal_th: แนะนำครอบครัว บอกความรู้สึก และบอกว่าชอบหรือคิดถึงอะไรได้
units.scenario: B is Minjun looking at Nam's family photos. He asks who each person is (grandparents, parents, siblings), how old they are and where they live, and how Nam feels living far from the family (glad, bored, worried, nervous).

lessons.topic: Grandparents, mum, sons and daughters
lessons.grammar: Talking about elders with 계세요 (review: 할머니는 방콕에 계세요); 엄마 / 아빠 (casual) vs 어머니 / 아버지 (polite)

lessons.topic: More feelings: glad, angry, bored, worried, nervous
lessons.grammar: Feeling adjectives for the speaker (기뻐요, 심심해요); 걱정돼요 / 긴장돼요 = I'm worried / nervous; 안 + feeling (안 심심해요)

lessons.topic: Nam's email to mum in Bangkok: Nam is fine in Seoul and has good Korean friends; sometimes Nam misses mum's food and the family, but is happy; mum should not worry and should stay healthy
lessons.grammar: Letter openings and closings; 보고 싶어요, feeling words, 그래도

units.title_th: ร้านกาแฟและร้านสะดวกซื้อ
units.goal_th: สั่งเครื่องดื่มที่ร้านกาแฟ และซื้อของที่ร้านสะดวกซื้อได้
units.scenario: B is a barista at a café, then a clerk at a convenience store. Nam orders drinks (iced or hot, how many cups, for here or to go), buys a snack and a triangle gimbap, answers whether a bag is needed and asks to have the food heated up.

lessons.topic: Ordering coffee: café, americano, latte, cups, order
lessons.grammar: N + native number + 잔 주세요 (아메리카노 두 잔 주세요); 주문 (order) heard as 주문하시겠어요?

lessons.topic: Hot or iced? Hot and cold things
lessons.grammar: 따뜻한 거 / 차가운 거 as fixed chunks; 뜨거워요 / 차가워요 for things you touch (Thai ร้อน / เย็น also covers the weather, Korean does not)

lessons.topic: For here or to go? Bread and waffles
lessons.grammar: 여기서 (= 여기에서) 먹어요 vs 가져가요; 포장 = packed to take away; N하고 N (review)

lessons.topic: At the convenience store: triangle gimbap, cup noodles, ice cream, banana milk, fish-cake bars
lessons.grammar: N 있어요? (review); N하고 N 주세요; the counter 개 (review); 바나나 우유 is a famous Korean drink

lessons.topic: At the counter: a plastic bag, do you need it?, please heat it up, 1+1 offers
lessons.grammar: N이/가 필요해요 (봉지 필요해요?); -아/어 주세요 (데워 주세요); 원 플러스 원 = buy one, get one free

lessons.topic: What would you like to drink? Green tea, cola, bottled water; bottles
lessons.grammar: V-고 싶어요 = want to (마시고 싶어요, 먹고 싶어요); native number + 병 (물 한 병)

lessons.topic: A café's summer notice board: a new bingsu menu, extra ice is free, a stamp card (ten stamps = one free americano), and a 1+1 event on Fridays
lessons.grammar: Prices and numbers, 부터 / 까지, short -요 sentences in a notice

units.title_th: โทรศัพท์และข้อความ
units.goal_th: รับโทรศัพท์ ส่งข้อความ ขอเบอร์หรือไอดีแชต และเปิดเบอร์มือถือในเกาหลีได้
units.scenario: B is Minjun, who calls Nam back after a missed call; they talk on the phone and exchange KakaoTalk details and photos. Later B is a clerk at a mobile phone shop helping Nam get a Korean SIM card.

lessons.topic: On the phone: hello, calling, answering, who is it?, may I speak to …
lessons.grammar: 여보세요 is only for the phone; N한테 전화해요 (call N); N 좀 바꿔 주세요 (please put N on)

lessons.topic: Messages: KakaoTalk, messages, sending, emoticons, send me the photo
lessons.grammar: N한테 N을/를 보내요 (민준 씨한테 메시지를 보내요); 한테 = to (a person); 사진 보내 주세요

lessons.topic: Exchanging contacts: number, please tell me, adding a friend, profile, call me
lessons.grammar: N 좀 알려 주세요; 친구 추가 (add as a friend in an app); 전화 주세요 = please call me

lessons.topic: At the phone shop: a phone, a SIM card, a mobile carrier, opening a line
lessons.grammar: N이/가 필요해요 (유심이 필요해요, review); N 있어요? (review); 개통 = getting a new line activated

lessons.topic: Can't talk now: a call, later, again, not answering
lessons.grammar: Negation 안 + verb (전화를 안 받아요); 이따가 (later today) vs 나중에 (some time later); 다시 전화해요

lessons.topic: Sound on the phone: speak up please, sound, ringtone, can you hear me?
lessons.grammar: -아/어 주세요 (크게 말해 주세요); 소리가 작아요 (review of 작아요); 들려요? = can you hear (me)?

lessons.topic: A KakaoTalk group chat of Nam's Korean class: someone asks who is free on Saturday for a class photo, people say where they are on the way, Nam sends the group photo, and everyone says thanks with emoticons
lessons.grammar: Short chat sentences, 한테, 보내요, 안 + verb

units.title_th: นับสิ่งของ (ลักษณนาม)
units.goal_th: นับสิ่งของ สัตว์ อาหาร และระยะเวลาด้วยลักษณนามที่ถูกต้องได้
units.scenario: B is a Korean friend helping Nam prepare a small dorm party. They make a shopping list and count everything with the right counter (공책 두 권, 종이 열 장, 장미 세 송이, 피자 두 판…), and talk about how long Nam has lived in Korea.

lessons.topic: Counting books, paper and pencils
lessons.grammar: Native number + 권 / 장 / 자루 (책 두 권, 종이 세 장, 연필 한 자루), like Thai เล่ม / แผ่น / แท่ง; 페이지 with Sino-Korean numbers (삼십 페이지)

lessons.topic: Counting clothes and shoes
lessons.grammar: Native number + 벌 / 켤레 (옷 한 벌, 양말 두 켤레), like Thai ชุด / คู่; N 주세요 (review)

lessons.topic: Counting animals and flowers
lessons.grammar: Native number + 마리 / 송이 (물고기 세 마리, 장미 열 송이), like Thai ตัว / ดอก

lessons.topic: Counting cars, bikes and machines
lessons.grammar: Native number + 대 (자동차 한 대, 자전거 두 대, 컴퓨터 세 대), like Thai คัน / เครื่อง

lessons.topic: Counting food at a restaurant and a shop: portions, plates, whole pizzas, cans
lessons.grammar: Sino-Korean number + 인분 (삼겹살 이 인분); native number + 접시 / 판 / 캔 (피자 한 판, 콜라 두 캔)

lessons.topic: How long? Months, weeks, during, every month
lessons.grammar: Sino-Korean number + 개월 (삼 개월); N 동안 (일주일 동안); 매달 = every month

lessons.topic: Nam's shopping list for a dorm party posted in the group chat: 3 portions of chicken, 10 cans of cola, 2 bags of snacks, 20 paper cups; each person brings one thing; something is not enough, so Minjun buys more
lessons.grammar: Counters with native and Sino-Korean numbers, N씩, -고 싶어요

units.title_th: กรอกข้อมูลส่วนตัว
units.goal_th: บอกข้อมูลส่วนตัวและกรอกแบบฟอร์มง่าย ๆ ได้ เช่น ชื่อ สัญชาติ วันเกิด อาชีพ
units.scenario: B is a receptionist at a Korean language school (or a gym). He helps Nam fill in a registration form: family name and name in English, nationality, date of birth, phone number and e-mail, job and marital status, then where to sign; finally he makes Nam's card.

lessons.topic: Name and nationality on a form: family name, nationality, name in English, male, female
lessons.grammar: Form words are nouns (성, 국적, 영문 이름); 국적이 어디예요? → 태국이에요 (review); Korean names: family name first

lessons.topic: Date of birth and age: date of birth, date, year, international age
lessons.grammar: Dates with Sino-Korean numbers: 이천육 년 삼월 오일 (년 / 월 / 일); 만 나이 = age counted from your birthday (Korea's official age since 2023)

lessons.topic: Contact details: e-mail, mobile number, in Korean letters, blank
lessons.grammar: N을/를 써 주세요 is in lesson 05; here N이/가 뭐예요? (이메일이 뭐예요?); 한글로 = in hangul; 빈칸 = blank on a form

lessons.topic: Job and marital status: occupation, married, single, graduate student
lessons.grammar: 직업이 뭐예요? → 학생이에요 (review); 기혼 / 미혼 are form words (in speech: 결혼했어요 is later)

lessons.topic: Signing and checking: signature, please write, tick, mark
lessons.grammar: -아/어 주세요 (여기에 써 주세요, 여기에 서명해 주세요); 체크 / 표시 하세요 = tick / mark it

lessons.topic: Getting a card made: make, issue, check, service window
lessons.grammar: N을/를 만들어요 (카드를 만들어요); 발급 = issue (a card); N 번 창구 (window number N, review of 번)

lessons.topic: A registration guide on a language-school website: where the registration desk is, what to write on the form (name in English, date of birth, phone number), the fee for one month, and when classes start
lessons.grammar: Form words, 부터 / 까지, -(으)세요 instructions

units.title_th: สุขภาพเบื้องต้น
units.goal_th: บอกว่าไม่สบายหรือเจ็บตรงไหน ซื้อยาที่ร้านขายยา และไปหาหมอได้
units.scenario: B is first a worried Korean friend, then a pharmacist. Nam says they feel unwell and where it hurts; the pharmacist asks about the symptoms, gives medicine, explains how many times a day to take it, and tells Nam to rest.

lessons.topic: Feeling sick: it hurts, a cold, a cough, sneezing
lessons.grammar: N이/가 아파요 (배가 아파요); 감기에 걸렸어요 is a fixed past form (learn as a chunk); 기침 / 재채기를 해요

lessons.topic: Where does it hurt? Upset stomach, throwing up, blood, a plaster
lessons.grammar: 어디가 아파요? → N이/가 아파요; 토해요 = throw up; 밴드 = plaster (a sticking plaster)

lessons.topic: At the pharmacy: medicine, painkillers, digestive medicine, fever medicine
lessons.grammar: 약을 먹어요 (Korean "eats" medicine, like Thai กินยา); 하루에 세 번 (하루 from ko-B5-r01 + 번); compounds with 제 "medicine" (진통제, 소화제, 해열제)

lessons.topic: At the hospital: doctor, nurse, injection, insurance
lessons.grammar: N에 가요 (병원에 가요, review); N 있어요? (보험 있어요?)

lessons.topic: Taking care: health, get some rest, get well soon, be careful
lessons.grammar: Polite requests with -(으)세요 (푹 쉬세요, 조심하세요); 빨리 나으세요 as a fixed wish

lessons.topic: Other symptoms: dizzy, itchy, mosquito bites, pain-relief patches
lessons.grammar: N이/가 가려워요; 모기에 물렸어요 (fixed past form); 파스 = pain-relief patch

lessons.topic: The instructions on a medicine bag from a Korean pharmacy: take the pills three times a day after meals, the liquid medicine only at night, drink a lot of water, do not drive, and rest well
lessons.grammar: -(으)세요 / -지 마세요 instructions; 하루에 N 번

units.title_th: อาหารริมทางและเดลิเวอรี
units.goal_th: สั่งอาหารริมทางและอาหารเดลิเวอรียอดนิยมของเกาหลีได้
units.scenario: B is first a street-food seller at a stall, then a Chinese-Korean restaurant taking a delivery order by phone. Nam orders snacks (어묵, 호떡), then orders jjajangmyeon and tangsuyuk for delivery, asks about the delivery fee and asks to leave the food at the door.

lessons.topic: Street food: blood sausage, fish cakes, sweet pancakes, fish-shaped buns
lessons.grammar: N 하나 주세요 / N 얼마예요? (review); 어묵 comes with free hot soup; 붕어빵 = 붕어 "carp" + 빵

lessons.topic: Chinese-Korean food: black-bean noodles, spicy seafood noodles, sweet-and-sour pork, dumplings
lessons.grammar: N하고 N 주세요; -고 싶어요 (review: 짬뽕 먹고 싶어요); 짜장면 is eaten on moving day and on 블랙데이 (14 April)

lessons.topic: More favourites: pig's trotters, boiled pork wraps, rice balls, ramen tteokbokki
lessons.grammar: Sino-Korean number + 인분 (족발 이 인분, review of ko-B9-05); N이/가 맛있어요 / 매워요 (review)

lessons.topic: Ordering delivery: delivery, delivery fee, please leave it at the door, doorbell
lessons.grammar: N이/가 얼마예요? (배달비가 얼마예요?); -아/어 주세요 (문 앞에 놓아 주세요); 놓아요 from ko-B1-06

lessons.topic: Rice and stews: rice soup, soft tofu stew, kimchi stew, soybean paste stew
lessons.grammar: N 하나 주세요; 찌개 is shared from the middle of the table, 국밥 is one bowl for one person

lessons.topic: Noodles: knife-cut noodles, banquet noodles, hand-torn dough soup, udon
lessons.grammar: N이/가 따뜻해요 / 뜨거워요 (review); 국수 = noodles: 칼 "knife" + 국수, 잔치 "party" + 국수

lessons.topic: Three short customer reviews in a delivery app: one says the chicken is crispy and the portion is generous, one says the jjamppong was too spicy and not so good, one thanks the rider for coming quickly in the rain
lessons.grammar: Adjectives in 해요체, 너무 / 정말 / 좀, 안 + adjective

units.title_th: เที่ยวเกาหลี
units.goal_th: พูดเรื่องการท่องเที่ยว ซื้อตั๋วรถ หาที่พัก แลกเงิน และขอให้คนช่วยถ่ายรูปได้
units.scenario: B is a ticket clerk at a bus terminal, then the owner of a small guesthouse (민박), then a friendly passer-by at a beach in Busan. Nam buys a bus ticket, checks in for one night, exchanges money and asks someone to take a photo.

lessons.topic: Travel and the airport: trip, airport, plane, luggage, plane ticket
lessons.grammar: N을/를 타요 (비행기를 타요, review); N에 가고 싶어요 (review of -고 싶어요)

lessons.topic: Places to stay: hotel, reservation, a family-run guesthouse, one night
lessons.grammar: N을/를 예약했어요 (fixed past form); 하룻밤 = one night; 민박 = a room in a local home

lessons.topic: Long-distance buses and trains: terminal, station, platform, bus ticket
lessons.grammar: N에서 N까지 (서울에서 부산까지, review); 몇 시 버스예요?; 버스표 = 버스 + 표 (표 from ko-A15-05)

lessons.topic: Places in Korea: Seoul, Busan, Jeju Island, beaches
lessons.grammar: N에 가고 싶어요 / N에서 N을/를 해요 (review); 제주도 = 제주 + 도 "island"

lessons.topic: Taking photos: please take a photo, one more (photo), beautiful, a tour guide
lessons.grammar: -아/어 주세요 (사진 좀 찍어 주세요); native number + 장 (한 장 더, 장 from ko-B9-01); 아름다워요

lessons.topic: Money for the trip: exchanging money, duty-free, banknotes, Korean won
lessons.grammar: N을/를 N(으)로 바꿔요 (Thai money into Korean won: … 원화로 바꿔 주세요); 지폐 = banknote, 원화 = Korean won (currency)

lessons.topic: Nam's travel blog post about the first day in Busan: arrives by train, the guesthouse is near Haeundae beach, eats raw fish at a market, watches the seagulls, and wants to come back
lessons.grammar: Places + 에 / 에서, -고 싶어요, descriptive adjectives

units.title_th: ขอความช่วยเหลือ
units.goal_th: ขอความช่วยเหลือ บอกปัญหาอย่างของหาย ของเสีย หรือหลงทาง และรับมือเหตุฉุกเฉินเบื้องต้นได้
units.scenario: B is a subway station staff member. Nam's wallet is gone and Nam is also a little lost; Nam explains what happened, describes the wallet (colour, what is inside) and gets help. Later B is a dormitory manager and Nam reports that the door will not open and there is no hot water.

lessons.topic: Emergencies: help!, police, are you all right?, dangerous, quickly
lessons.grammar: 도와주세요! (fixed); 빨리 와 주세요 (-아/어 주세요); 괜찮으세요? (honorific of 괜찮아요?); 위험해요!; Korean emergency numbers 112 (police) and 119 (ambulance, fire)

lessons.topic: My wallet is gone: lost property, where, pickpocket, I found it
lessons.grammar: N이/가 없어요 (지갑이 없어요, review of 없어요); 어디서 = 어디에서; 찾았어요 (fixed past form)

lessons.topic: Things that don't work: it doesn't work, it won't open, no water comes out, out of order, repairs
lessons.grammar: Negation 안 + verb (안 열려요, 물이 안 나와요); 고장이에요 (고장 from ko-A15-04); 수리 = repair

lessons.topic: I'm lost: where am I?, map, nearby, police station, I don't know the way
lessons.grammar: 여기가 어디예요?; N 근처에 N이/가 있어요? (review of 있어요); 길을 몰라요 (몰라요 from ko-A1-04)

lessons.topic: Complaints in the dorm or a hotel: a smell, bugs, noise; please fix it; asking a favour
lessons.grammar: N이/가 너무 + adjective (review); -아/어 주세요 (고쳐 주세요); 부탁해요 = please, I'm counting on you

lessons.topic: Fire and alarms: fire!, alarm bell, police officer, call 119
lessons.grammar: 불이야! (fixed shout); N에 전화하세요 (일일구에 전화하세요); 경찰관 = police officer (경찰 = the police)

lessons.topic: A "lost wallet" poster Nam puts up in the dormitory: a brown wallet gone on Friday evening near the school shop, with a student card and a transport card inside; if anyone has it, please contact Nam; Nam thanks people in advance
lessons.grammar: Notice style, colours and descriptions, 연락 주세요

units.title_th: ไปบ้านเพื่อนชาวเกาหลี
units.goal_th: ไปเยี่ยมบ้านคนเกาหลีอย่างมีมารยาท ทักทาย กินอาหาร และขอบคุณเจ้าของบ้านได้
units.scenario: B is Minjun, who invites Nam to his family's home for dinner. Nam brings a gift, greets the family politely, takes off shoes, waits for the elders to start eating, joins a toast, and thanks the family when leaving.

lessons.topic: Arriving at a Korean home: a gift, excuse me (coming in), come in, taking off shoes
lessons.grammar: 실례합니다 when entering; honorific -(으)세요 (들어오세요); N을/를 벗어요 (신발을 벗어요)

lessons.topic: At the table: please sit, eat a lot, first, waiting
lessons.grammar: Honorific requests (앉으세요, 많이 드세요); 먼저 = first (할머니가 먼저 드세요; the oldest person starts eating first); 기다려요

lessons.topic: Greeting the family: cheers, greeting, shaking hands, bowing
lessons.grammar: N을/를 + verb (고개를 숙여요); 인사해요 = greet / bow (Thai ไหว้ vs the Korean bow); 건배! when glasses meet

lessons.topic: Friendly gestures: waving, finger hearts, clapping, high fives
lessons.grammar: N을/를 + verb (손을 흔들어요); 박수 and 하이파이브 used as nouns here (박수! 하이파이브!), the verb 치다 comes later

lessons.topic: Home food: Korean food, side dishes, glass noodles, kimchi-making, home cooking
lessons.grammar: N에 N을/를 먹어요 (생일에 잡채를 먹어요); 반찬 are free and refillable in Korean restaurants; 집밥 = home-cooked meal

lessons.topic: Leaving: come again, go safely, next time, thank you for having me
lessons.grammar: Set phrases when leaving (또 오세요, 조심히 가세요); 다음에 = next time; 신세 졌어요 = thank you for your kindness (fixed)

lessons.topic: Nam's short blog essay "Korean customs that surprised me": at first it was strange that people ask your age, give things with two hands and wait for the oldest person to eat first; now Nam understands why, and especially likes eating home-cooked food with Minjun's family
lessons.grammar: 처음에는 … 지금은 … with 은/는 for contrast, 하지만, 그래서

units.title_th: ไปดูหนัง
units.goal_th: ชวนเพื่อนไปดูหนัง จองตั๋ว เลือกที่นั่ง ซื้อขนม และเล่าความรู้สึกหลังดูหนังได้
units.scenario: B is a Korean friend and then a cinema clerk. They choose a film (horror, comedy, action, animation), book tickets and seats, buy popcorn, and after the film say how they felt about it.

lessons.topic: What kind of film? Cinema, horror, comedy, action, animation
lessons.grammar: 무슨 영화 보고 싶어요? (-고 싶어요, review); N 영화 (공포 영화, 액션 영화)

lessons.topic: Booking tickets: booking, sold out, seats, screening
lessons.grammar: N을/를 예매해요; 매진이에요 = sold out; 좌석 = seat (on tickets and signs)

lessons.topic: Choosing seats: seat, middle, front row, back row
lessons.grammar: 자리 = seat, place (everyday word); 가운데 자리 주세요; 맨 앞 / 맨 뒤 = the very front / back

lessons.topic: Cinema snacks: popcorn, nachos, dried squid, a combo set
lessons.grammar: N하고 N 주세요; 세트 = combo set; 오징어 = squid (dried squid is a classic Korean cinema snack)

lessons.topic: After the film: moving, scary, boring, tears
lessons.grammar: N이/가 무서워요 / 지루해요; 감동이에요 = it was moving; 눈물이 나요 = I cried

lessons.topic: Talking about a film: director, spoilers, what time is the film?, going to see it
lessons.grammar: 몇 시 영화예요? (review of 몇); V-러 가요 = go to do (보러 가요, 먹으러 가요)

lessons.topic: Nam's short film review on a movie app about a new film (개봉 영화), written in the present tense: the story is fun and moving, the ending is beautiful, Nam gives it five stars and strongly recommends it
lessons.grammar: Adjectives for feelings, 정말 / 너무, -고 싶어요
